workflowRecommendation: One implementer, one PR, TDD: write the config.test.ts and cli/__tests__/index.test.ts cases first and watch them fail, then change config.ts, then the AGENTS.md sentence. Run only the two touched test files plus `bunx tsc --noEmit` and `bunx biome check` on the touched files; CI runs the suite. One behaviour commit is enough (`daemon: bound every timer setting at the 32-bit setTimeout limit (LEGION-46)`).
concerns: SPEC DELTA 1: slow_command_timeout_seconds is a real setTimeout delay (packages/daemon/src/state/fetch.ts:103 `setTimeout(() => kill("budget"), limitMs)`, limitMs = slowCommandTimeoutSeconds*1000 via index.ts:295 and processes.ts:2431). The spec's Summary lists five *_seconds keys and omits it; it is bounded here. Above the bound every boot probe and workspace clone would be killed at 1 ms: the probes fail 'transiently' forever and the launch hold never releases.

SPEC DELTA 2: the root/controller registration deadline is ONE timer for the PRODUCT workerBootTimeoutSeconds * 1000 * workerBootRegistrationDeadlineIntervals (processes.ts:1575-1579 and 1607-1611 -> boundedWait -> createCancellableSleep -> setTimeout). Per-key bounds leave it open (2147483 s x default 3 intervals clamps to 1 ms and retires every booting root three times -> launch-failed). A post-resolve product check is added; message names both keys.

SPEC DELTA 3 (documentation accuracy): linger_hours never reaches setTimeout. processes.ts:2105-2106 and 2551-2552 write lingerUntil = new Date(now + lingerHours * HOUR_MS).toISOString(), and index.ts:722-731 sweeps it with a fixed setInterval comparing Date.parse(lingerUntil) <= now. It is bounded at MAX_TIMER_HOURS anyway (spec Acceptance 1; Rejected: 'bounding only the keys observed to matter'), and the bound forecloses a real latent crash (hours*HOUR_MS past the Date range, ~2.4e9 h, makes toISOString() throw RangeError at beginLinger). Code comments, the error text, and AGENTS.md must describe it as a duration key under the shared rule, not as a timer delay.

The idle-retire refusal text changes: '(the largest whole number of seconds whose millisecond delay fits a 32-bit timer)' is dropped from the message (the explanation lives on the constant's doc comment and in AGENTS.md; the shared message is the spec's `<key> must be at most <bound>`), while the '; use 0 to disable idle retirement' hint is kept via checkAtMost's optional hint. Two existing full-message assertions (config.test.ts:560-562 and 574-576) must change; everything else in that test stays.

A boundary test for worker_boot_timeout_seconds at 2147483 with the DEFAULT intervals (3) is refused by the product check, by design. The per-key boundary pair therefore uses resync_interval_seconds (no product interaction, and it is the one key whose env value is multiplied into ms only in the return statement, so it is where a unit mistake in the post-resolve check would hide).

Bun 1.3.14 on this machine confirmed the premise: setTimeout(fn, 2147484*1000) fired after 5 ms with `TimeoutOverflowWarning: 2147484000 does not fit into a 32-bit signed integer. Timeout duration was set to 1.`; setTimeout(fn, 2147483*1000) stayed pending. Math.floor(2147483/3600) = 596 (= 2145600 s).

design.constants: Replace lines 188-193 (MAX_WORKER_IDLE_RETIRE_SECONDS doc + const) with two module-private constants: `const MAX_TIMER_SECONDS = 2_147_483;` — doc: the largest whole number of seconds whose millisecond delay fits the signed 32-bit delay setTimeout accepts (`seconds * 1000 <= 2_147_483_647`); beyond it Bun clamps the delay to 1 ms and the timer fires at once, so every duration setting that reaches a timer is refused above it rather than clamped — and `const MAX_TIMER_HOURS = Math.floor(MAX_TIMER_SECONDS / 3600);` (596; computed so it cannot drift). Not exported: tests pin the literals 2147483/596 exactly as the existing idle-retire test pins 2147483 — the literal in the test is the guard.
design.sharedCheck: One new helper beside readPositiveInteger — the only place the bound message is produced: `function checkAtMost(number: number, field: string, max: number, hint?: string): number { if (number > max) throw new Error(`${field} must be at most ${max}${hint === undefined ? "" : `; ${hint}`}`); return number; }`. Chosen over a readBoundedSeconds wrapper because the existing code shape is (a) a `check*` rule function every source funnels through (checkIdleRetireSeconds, PR #973) and (b) inline `> 65535` port checks that are literally this shape; a wrapper would add a fourth parser variant while leaving the env twin and the post-resolve loop to duplicate the bound.
design.readPositiveInteger: Add an optional third parameter `max?: number`: after the positive-integer check, `return max === undefined ? number : checkAtMost(number, field, max);`. Same for `parseEnvPositiveInteger(value, field, max?)`.
design.fileLoop: loadConfigFromFile lines 721-736: give the table an optional third column and pass it through — `readPositiveInteger(config[fileKey], fileKey, max)`. Rows: linger_hours -> MAX_TIMER_HOURS; worker_stop_timeout_seconds, tree_stop_timeout_seconds, worker_boot_timeout_seconds, worker_rpc_timeout_seconds, slow_command_timeout_seconds -> MAX_TIMER_SECONDS; admission_cap, worker_cap, max_recursion_depth, max_fix_attempts, worker_boot_registration_deadline_intervals -> no max. TYPING HAZARD: destructuring `[fileKey, configKey, max]` from an `as const` union of 2- and 3-tuples errors on the 2-tuples; type the table `ReadonlyArray<readonly [string, string, number?]>` (or give every row three entries) and drop `as const`.
design.fileResync: line 746-749: `readPositiveInteger(config.resync_interval_seconds, "resync_interval_seconds", MAX_TIMER_SECONDS)`; the `* 1000` on line 750 stays.
design.filePortsCleanup: lines 673-677 and 751-755: `readPositiveInteger(config.port, "port", 65535)` / `readPositiveInteger(config.worker_stream_port, "worker_stream_port", 65535)` replace the inline `> 65535` throws — identical messages (`port must be at most 65535`, `worker_stream_port must be at most 65535`, pinned by config.test.ts:709-711). This is the adjacent cleanup the new `max` parameter causes; nothing else about ports changes (the env-side `LEGION_DAEMON_PORT must be a valid TCP port` messages stay).
design.envParsers: resolveDaemonConfig: pass the bound as the third argument to parseEnvPositiveInteger for LEGION_LINGER_HOURS (MAX_TIMER_HOURS, line 966), LEGION_RESYNC_INTERVAL_SECONDS (line 978), LEGION_WORKER_STOP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (984), LEGION_TREE_STOP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (993), LEGION_WORKER_BOOT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (1002), LEGION_WORKER_RPC_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (1020), LEGION_SLOW_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (1038) — all MAX_TIMER_SECONDS except linger. Messages come out as `LEGION_<KEY> must be at most <bound>`.
design.postResolve: Lines 1067-1089. (1) Hoist the ms normalization above the check: `const resyncIntervalMsValue = resyncIntervalMs.value * (resyncIntervalMs.source === "env" ? 1000 : 1);` and use it in the return (line 1137). (2) Change `lifecycleNumbers` to `Record<string, { value: number; max?: number }>` with max on lingerHours (MAX_TIMER_HOURS), resyncIntervalMs (MAX_TIMER_SECONDS * 1000 — the field is milliseconds), workerStopTimeoutSeconds, treeStopTimeoutSeconds, workerBootTimeoutSeconds, workerRpcTimeoutSeconds, slowCommandTimeoutSeconds (MAX_TIMER_SECONDS); loop body: positive-integer check as today, then `if (max !== undefined) checkAtMost(value, field, max);`. These camelCase-named refusals are the only guard for a cliOverride, exactly like the existing `workerIdleRetireSeconds must be at most 2147483` (config.test.ts:582). (3) After `checkIdleRetireSeconds(...)`, the product check: `checkAtMost(workerBootTimeoutSeconds.value * workerBootRegistrationDeadlineIntervals.value, "worker_boot_timeout_seconds * worker_boot_registration_deadline_intervals", MAX_TIMER_SECONDS);` with a comment naming processes.ts's registration deadlines as the single timer that multiplies them. Snake_case here follows the existing cross-key post-resolve messages (`worker_stream_port must differ from port`).
design.idleRetire: checkIdleRetireSeconds (lines 334-344): keep the non-negative/-0 check; replace the own-constant throw with `return checkAtMost(number, field, MAX_TIMER_SECONDS, "use 0 to disable idle retirement");`. Resulting text: `worker_idle_retire_seconds must be at most 2147483; use 0 to disable idle retirement` (and the LEGION_/camelCase variants). readIdleRetireSeconds/parseEnvIdleRetireSeconds unchanged.
design.staleComments: Rewrite every comment that says idle-retire is the only bounded key or names the old constant: DaemonConfig.workerIdleRetireSeconds doc lines 109-110 (`at most MAX_TIMER_SECONDS`); checkIdleRetireSeconds doc 329-333; readIdleRetireSeconds doc 346-348 (drop 'and the one with an upper bound'); loop comment 737-738 ('the key carries an upper bound no other lifecycle number has' is now false — the reason it stays outside the loop is only that 0 is valid); post-resolve comment 1086-1088 likewise. Comments describe current behaviour, not history.
design.notTouched: The triplicated positive-integer check (readPositiveInteger / parseEnvPositiveInteger / lifecycleNumbers loop) is pre-existing duplication this change does not cause; leave it. No consumer (processes.ts, worker-boot-watchdog.ts, index.ts, state/fetch.ts) changes: the fix is refusing the value at the door, never clamping or guarding at the timer.
